articles.title: John Roesch Exits Meridian to Start Roesch Real Estate Group
articles.narrative: John Roesch, a veteran retail leasing broker, has departed Meridian Retail Leasing after nearly a decade to establish his own firm, Roesch Real Estate Group (RREG). The new company will initially concentrate on retail leasing, with plans to expand into investment sales, aiming to bring institutional-level execution to the middle market. Roesch emphasized that his departure was driven by a readiness to lead his own venture, building on the experience and confidence gained at Meridian.

articles.title: More Commercial Real Estate Owners See Value in Special Servicing Platforms
articles.narrative: The article discusses the growing trend of commercial real estate owners launching special servicing platforms, leveraging their deep market expertise to resolve troubled assets. RXR is the latest firm to enter this space with its REX Loan Services platform, approved by Fitch Ratings and Morningstar. The move is seen as a way to complement RXR's lending business and utilize its extensive experience in the office sector, which still faces significant distress. While concerns about potential conflicts of interest exist, particularly when a competitor acts as a special servicer, proponents argue that owner-operators bring unique insights that can expedite solutions for defaulted CMBS loans.

articles.title: From Builder to Partner
articles.narrative: This article profiles Wharton Smith Construction, highlighting its strategic growth in New York City's commercial construction market. The firm, led by founder Elliott Mishan, emphasizes building internal capabilities—people, systems, and infrastructure—to handle increasingly complex projects, including office fit-outs, corporate headquarters, retail environments, medical facilities, and adaptive reuse. Wharton Smith focuses on maintaining high service levels while expanding project scale and volume, leveraging a dedicated team structure and advanced preconstruction processes. Senior Estimator Zackery Batt and Senior Project Manager Billy Collins are noted for their contributions to modernizing budgeting and ensuring disciplined project execution, respectively.

articles.title: Sunday Summary: Unpacking the Near-Collapse at Pfizer HQ
articles.narrative: This article is a weekly summary covering several distinct real estate news items in New York City. It reports on the partial collapse of steel support structures at the former Pfizer headquarters, an office-to-residential conversion project by Metro Loft and David Werner Real Estate Investments, which caused five floors to cave in. The incident, which thankfully resulted in no injuries, has drawn significant scrutiny to the developer's construction practices. The summary also highlights a strong week for office leasing, with major law firms and media companies expanding or renewing their footprints, and notable retail leasing activity including new restaurant and store openings. Finally, it touches on key personnel hires and promotions within the real estate industry.

articles.title: Dallas office market continues to stabilize as tenant demand remains positive
articles.narrative: The Dallas office market demonstrated continued stabilization and positive momentum in the first half of 2026, driven by strong tenant demand for high-quality, amenity-rich office spaces, according to a JLL report. While much of the activity involved companies relocating within the metro rather than expanding, this flight-to-quality trend has fueled development in desirable submarkets like Uptown and supported rent growth for premium properties. Despite a selective investment market, Dallas continues to benefit from significant corporate migration, with over 100 companies relocating headquarters to the region since 2018, including a recent major announcement from Samsung. The market is projected to maintain steady performance, with positive absorption and declining vacancy rates through the end of 2026.
articles.market_intelligence: The Dallas office market is characterized by a flight-to-quality trend, with companies favoring newer, high-quality buildings with modern amenities. This has led to rent growth in Trophy office properties and a widening pricing gap between new construction and mid-priced office buildings. The investment market is highly selective, with capital directed towards well-leased, high-performing assets in strong submarkets. Many owners are opting for refinancing or recapitalizations instead of selling at discounted values. Corporate migration continues to be a significant driver, with over 100 companies relocating headquarters to the Dallas-Fort Worth metro area since 2018.

articles.title: Inside the Underwriting Process: What Affordable Housing Lenders Look for That Developers Don’t Always See
articles.narrative: This article, authored by a managing director at Bridgewater Bank, offers an inside look into the underwriting process for affordable housing projects from a lender's perspective. It emphasizes that lenders evaluate not just the vision but also the readiness and execution capacity of a development team, scrutinizing project assumptions, funding reliability, and organizational bandwidth. The author highlights the importance of conservative operating assumptions and a deep understanding of compliance and mission alignment, asserting that strong projects are built on transparent and responsive partnerships.

articles.title: The Langley multifamily development opens in Houston
articles.narrative: The Langley, a 20-story luxury multifamily high-rise developed by StreetLights Residential and Hunt Real Estate, has completed construction in Houston. Located near Rice University, the building features 134 residences for lease, with two- and three-bedroom homes ranging from 2,165 to 3,396 square feet and monthly rents starting at $9,480. The development emphasizes timeless architectural principles, high-end finishes, and a boutique scale with only eight residences per floor to create an intimate and private living experience.

data_points.notable_features: Located at the intersection of Boulevard Oaks and Southampton neighborhoods, near Rice University. Features 10- to 12-foot ceilings, wide-plank oak flooring, custom cabinetry, natural stone finishes, and smart-home technology.
data_points.project_notes: Residences range from 2,165 to 3,396 square feet. Designed with a classical architectural framework, incorporating brick, stone, and custom metalwork.

articles.title: Texas Icon Nikhil Dhanani: Building an Institutional-Grade Real Estate Platform from a Family Enterprise
articles.narrative: This article profiles Nikhil Dhanani, President of Dhanani Private Equity Group (DPEG), highlighting his role in transforming a family-owned operation into a vertically integrated, institutional-grade real estate platform. Over the past decade, Dhanani has been instrumental in scaling DPEG's assets under management from approximately $20 million to over $2.5 billion, diversifying its portfolio across retail, multifamily, and mixed-use developments. His leadership emphasizes disciplined execution, proactive asset management, and strategic repositioning of assets to create long-term value, particularly through attracting national and lifestyle brands to DPEG's retail centers.

articles.title: Marcus & Millichap closes sale of 25,113-square-foot shopping center in Houston
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap has facilitated the sale of Seabrook Shopping Center, a multi-tenant retail property in Houston's Bay Area. The 25,113-square-foot center was sold by a local investor to a buyer who was introduced to the opportunity through an existing relationship after a previous acquisition in the Houston area. The property offers significant lease-up potential, with approximately 19,000 square feet of available space, which is expected to increase long-term net operating income.

data_points.notable_features: Located in the Bay Area near Space Center Houston, with visibility along a high-traffic corridor carrying over 19,000 vehicles per day.

articles.title: The near-collapse that rattled NYC’s conversion boom
articles.narrative: A structural incident at the former Pfizer headquarters, currently undergoing New York City's largest office-to-residential conversion, caused a temporary evacuation and raised concerns about the project's stability. While engineers quickly shored up the affected area and developers plan to rebuild 15 floors, the event has prompted questions about engineering and construction oversight in large-scale conversions. The incident is expected to lead to increased scrutiny for future office-to-residential projects, which are a key component of New York's housing and obsolete office building strategy.

data_points.notable_features: Largest office-to-residential conversion in New York City.
data_points.project_notes: Project involves converting the former Pfizer campus into apartments. A structural incident occurred during construction, requiring temporary shoring and plans to rebuild approximately 15 floors.

articles.title: A surge in overbidding, an office boom flows south and a dead dead-mall deal
articles.narrative: San Francisco's housing market is experiencing an unprecedented surge in overbidding, with 144 homes selling for at least $1 million over list price in the first half of this year, a 1,700% increase from the previous year. This intense competition is driven by new wealth from the artificial intelligence sector and a booming stock market, creating a challenging environment for even affluent buyers. Meanwhile, the city's commercial real estate market is seeing a peculiar recovery, with high demand for trophy office spaces despite a citywide vacancy rate of 28-32%. The AI boom is also driving San Francisco companies to expand into larger campuses in Silicon Valley, where office vacancy rates have fallen to 14.1%. In other news, the planned acquisition of the 1.2 million-square-foot San Francisco Centre Mall by Presidio Bay Ventures and the Prado Group has fallen through, returning the property to the market.

data_points.project_notes: The property was seized by lenders in November through a $134 million credit bid in a foreclosure auction.

articles.title: Net Lease Cap Rates Tick Upward in Q2 2026
articles.narrative: Overall single-tenant net lease cap rates saw a slight increase in the second quarter of 2026, rising two basis points to 6.82%, according to The Boulder Group. This uptick was primarily driven by retail and industrial sectors, which experienced increases of five and ten basis points respectively, while office cap rates held steady. The shift is attributed to the Federal Reserve's revised interest rate projections, which removed an anticipated rate cut and introduced the possibility of a hike later in the year, influencing investor calculations for the latter half of 2026. Despite these changes, transaction volume is expected to remain stable, with continued investor interest in the fundamental appeal of net lease assets, potentially bolstered by corporate sale-leaseback activity.
articles.market_intelligence: A headquarters building in the Bronx traded in June at a 6.11% cap rate.

articles.title: Chicago's Older Apartments Are Running Out Of Room To Raise Rent
articles.narrative: Chicago's Class-C apartment market is facing significant challenges despite overall multifamily tailwinds, as rising operating costs for insurance, property taxes, and utilities are outpacing rent growth for older properties. This squeeze on margins is particularly acute for vintage stock, where some investors who focused on cosmetic upgrades in recent years deferred vital maintenance, making these properties harder to sell. While rent-by-necessity rates have increased substantially, they are now approaching affordability limits for workforce tenants, compressing the runway for further rent hikes. The market is seeing a return to more experienced operators who are selectively pursuing value-add opportunities, often with below-market rents or assumable low-rate debt, as new buyers face higher financing costs.
